bull.b: Growth in recurring revenue and a 169-system validated base indicate customers are moving from initial placements into repeat testing. This installed-base model can improve revenue visibility because consumables and service usage rise as systems are routinely used.

The sharp improvement in gross and service margins shows that execution and cost productivity are beginning to improve the economics of the platform. If sustained, higher service profitability and better system margins can support a durable path toward stronger overall margins.

Consumable growth above 20% and record quarterly volume demonstrate increasing routine use of Growth Direct systems after placement. This supports the company’s recurring-revenue model and suggests broader adoption can compound revenue as the installed base expands.

bear.b: Large net and adjusted EBITDA losses show that revenue growth and recent margin gains have not yet translated into operating scale. Continued losses can delay self-funded expansion, require additional capital, and leave the business exposed if profitability improvement takes longer than planned.

Dependence on future debt access and potential warrant proceeds indicates that current operations and planned investments are not fully supported by internal cash generation. Funding execution therefore remains important to sustaining operations while the company pursues profitability.

Negative product margin means system sales currently dilute profitability even as service economics improve. Until product margins reach breakeven and expand, additional placements may not generate sufficient contribution to offset operating expenses or accelerate the path to company-wide profitability.
